scholarships.name: Canada Postdoctoral Research Award (CPRA)
scholarships.provider: Government of Canada / CIHR / NSERC / SSHRC
scholarships.program_type: Tri-agency postdoctoral fellowship (CRTAS suite)
scholarships.deadline: CIHR: September 17 | NSERC: October 17 | SSHRC: September 11 (annual)
application_period: Applications open approximately 4–5 months before deadline - check agency websites

raw_items: Must hold or expect to hold a doctorate or health professional degree before award start date
Must NOT hold or be on leave from a tenure-track or tenured faculty position
PhD/degree completion no more than 3 years before September 1 of application year (extensions possible for parental leave, illness, military service, etc.)
International applicants: must be currently enrolled in or have completed doctorate at a Canadian institution, OR conducting postdoc at a Canadian institution - as of application deadline
Up to 20% of awards available to international applicants
Can be held at Canadian institutions OR abroad (up to 30% available internationally - Canadian citizens/PRs only for international tenure)
Cannot have previously received a postdoctoral award from CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC (including old Banting)
Maximum 3 applications allowed
Research program must be predominantly research-oriented and significantly different from doctoral thesis

benefits: Can be held at academic research institutions, research hospitals, colleges, NGOs, or Indigenous organizations in Canada or abroad (conditions apply)
Additional supplements may be available for priority areas, Black postdoctoral researchers, and Indigenous researchers
scholarships.target_group: Outstanding early-career researchers (within 3 years of PhD) from Canada and internationally who are pursuing postdoctoral research at Canadian institutions, across health, natural sciences, engineering, and social sciences.
scholarships.description: The Canada Postdoctoral Research Award (CPRA) is the successor to the discontinued Banting Postdoctoral Fellowship, providing CAD $70,000/year for 2 years to outstanding postdoctoral researchers. Administered jointly by CIHR, NSERC, and SSHRC, it supports researchers at Canadian and select international institutions. Up to 20% of awards are available to international applicants who are enrolled or conducting postdocs at Canadian institutions.
application_process: Select the funding agency matching your research field: CIHR (health), NSERC (natural sciences/engineering), SSHRC (social sciences/humanities)
Check institutional deadlines - your host institution may have an internal nomination deadline well before the agency deadline
Apply via the relevant agency online platform: CIHR (ResearchNET), NSERC (online system), SSHRC (Registration and login)
International applicants must apply through a Canadian institution - direct applications not accepted
Submission must be complete and on time - late applications are not accepted
Results announced: March 31
Contacts: CIHR: support-soutien@cihr-irsc.gc.ca | NSERC: nsercscholarships-boursescrsng@nserc-crsng.gc.ca | SSHRC: fellowships@sshrc-crsh.gc.ca

scholarships.name: Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes - Undergraduate & Master's Scholarship
scholarships.provider: Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes / German Academic Scholarship Foundation
scholarships.program_type: Merit-based full scholarship for enrolled students at German universities
scholarships.deadline: Nomination-based - no fixed open application; admitted via university nomination or self-nomination in first two semesters
application_period: Applications via nomination only - contact your German university liaison professor (Vertrauensdozent)
important_dates: Nomination deadlines vary by nominating body (school, university, government)
Selection seminars held multiple times per year
German citizenship or permanent residence in Germany often required - international students studying at German universities may be eligible

raw_items: Currently enrolled at an accredited German university or Fachhochschule
Outstanding academic achievement (top percentile)
Strong extra-curricular engagement and social commitment
Must be nominated by a liaison professor (Vertrauensdozent), school/university, or apply via self-nomination in first two semesters
All nationalities studying at German institutions may be eligible - confirm current rules with Studienstiftung
Must not be beyond the 3rd semester at time of first application

benefits: International study support (additional grants for semesters abroad)
Extensive non-material support: summer academies, seminars, networking events
Access to Studienstiftung academic programme (lectures, workshops, research groups)
scholarships.target_group: Outstanding university students of all nationalities studying at accredited German higher education institutions, who demonstrate exceptional academic ability and a commitment to contributing to society.
scholarships.description: The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes is Germany's oldest, largest and most prestigious scholarship foundation, supporting around 13,300 students annually across all disciplines at German universities. Admission is exclusively by nomination. International students enrolled at German universities may be eligible.
application_process: Identify a Vertrauensdozent (liaison professor) at your German university who can nominate you
OR self-nominate during your first or second semester via the Studienstiftung self-nomination portal
OR be nominated by your German school (Abitur route)
Submit nomination documents through the nominator - Studienstiftung contacts you for the next steps
Attend a two-day selection seminar
No direct application to Studienstiftung without a nomination

scholarships.name: Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes - Doctoral Scholarship
scholarships.provider: Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes / German Academic Scholarship Foundation
scholarships.program_type: Merit-based doctoral scholarship at German universities
scholarships.deadline: Rolling - calls open approximately 8 months before each selection meeting (Oct 1, Feb 1, Jun 1, Oct 1 of each year)
important_dates: Call opening dates 2027: February 1, June 1, October 1
Maximum 300 complete applications accepted per call - applications close when quota reached
Selection process: ~4–6 months from submission to decision
Applications submitted physically to: Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes, Promotionsförderung, Ahrstraße 41, 53175 Bonn

raw_items: Doctoral candidate accepted at a German university (or German citizen doing PhD abroad)
All nationalities eligible - nationality is irrelevant
Last academic degree completed no more than 4 years before application
Scholarship must start within 6 months of funding approval
Must be in early-stage doctoral research - not near completion
Full-time doctoral research only (no part-time doctorate)
Cannot combine with other major doctoral funding body scholarships
Must have a well-developed research exposé
Outstanding academic grades in all prior degrees
Evidence of extra-curricular and societal commitment

benefits: Health insurance subsidy: up to €100/month if not covered by mandatory insurance
Conference and research trip travel allowances
Tuition fee subsidy up to €10,000/year for doctorates outside home country
Access to Studienstiftung academic programme (summer academies, workshops)
scholarships.target_group: Highly qualified doctoral candidates at German universities (all nationalities) with ambitious dissertation projects, excellent academic records, and strong societal engagement.
scholarships.description: The Studienstiftung doctoral scholarship supports ~350 new doctoral scholars per year across all disciplines at German universities. Open to all nationalities enrolled at German institutions. Rolling applications throughout the year with four selection meetings; calls are capped at 300 applications each.
application_process: Wait for a call to open (Oct 1, Feb 1, Jun 1, or Oct 1)
Prepare application: cover sheet, applicant questionnaire, supervisor questionnaire, degree certificates, CV, and a detailed research exposé (max 20 pages)
Submit all documents as a single physical package (no double-sided prints, no binders) to the Bonn address
Also propose names of two academic reviewers for the review phase
Stage 1: preliminary review (~4 weeks)
Stage 2: written review by two external academics
Stage 3: selection board decision (meets 4x/year)
Contact: promotion@studienstiftung.de

scholarships.name: Studienstiftung ERP Fellowship Programme
scholarships.provider: Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes / German Academic Scholarship Foundation
scholarships.program_type: Study/research stay at US universities - transatlantic programme
fields: All disciplines except pure artistic studies (music, art, drama, film)
scholarships.deadline: September 20 annually (for the following academic year)
important_dates: Not eligible: study at Harvard Kennedy School (covered by McCloy)
German citizenship NOT mandatory - international students may be eligible, see: https://www.studienstiftung.de/infos-fuer-studierende/voraussetzungen/

raw_items: Hold at least a Bachelor's degree by the application deadline
Last university degree (including doctorate) no more than 5 years old
Excellent academic grades
Interest in public service orientation (NGO, international organizations, ministries, think tanks)
NOT studying at Harvard Kennedy School (use McCloy instead)
Admission to a US university not required at time of application
Prior Studienstiftung membership not required
International applicants (non-German): check eligibility at studienstiftung.de/infos-fuer-studierende/voraussetzungen/

benefits: Tuition fee grant up to USD 25,000 per academic year
Admission to Studienstiftung network and academic programmes
Membership in worldwide ERP alumni network
scholarships.target_group: Outstanding graduates from all disciplines (non-arts) seeking a 1–2 year Master's or PhD study/research stay at leading US universities, with an interest in public service, policy, or transatlantic engagement.
scholarships.description: The ERP Fellowship Programme funds 10–20 exceptional graduates per year for Master's or PhD studies at top US universities (excluding HKS), with generous stipend and tuition support. Funded by Germany's post-Marshall Plan ERP assets and designed to strengthen transatlantic ties. International (non-German) applicants may be eligible.
application_process: Download application form (German) from the Studienstiftung ERP page
Submit completed PDF application by email to erp@studienstiftung.de by September 20
Shortlisted applicants invited to a selection seminar
Apply separately and independently to US universities
Contact: erp@studienstiftung.de

scholarships.name: Studienstiftung McCloy Scholarship Programme
scholarships.provider: Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes / German Academic Scholarship Foundation
scholarships.program_type: 2-year Master's programme at Harvard Kennedy School
important_dates: Up to 6 scholarships awarded per year
Applicants must also apply directly to Harvard Kennedy School
International (non-German) applicants: check eligibility at studienstiftung.de

raw_items: Open to all disciplines
Must hold Bachelor's, Master's, Diplom, or state examination with grade "good" or above (law: "fully satisfactory")
Last university degree no more than 5 years old at application deadline (November 1)
Academic excellence, international experience, communication skills
Interest in practice-oriented solutions and public service
Admission to Harvard Kennedy School NOT required at time of application
Prior Studienstiftung membership not required
International applicants: check eligibility via studienstiftung.de

benefits: Tuition fee reduction to €10,000 per academic year at HKS
Compulsory public-sector internship between first and second year (supported)
Access to Studienstiftung and Haniel Foundation networks
Access to global McCloy alumni network
Emergency fund support (if other scholarships unsuccessful)
scholarships.target_group: Exceptional graduates of all disciplines with strong academic records, international experience, and a commitment to public service who aspire to study at Harvard Kennedy School in a 2-year Master's programme.
scholarships.description: The McCloy Scholarship Programme enables up to 6 outstanding graduates per year to pursue a 2-year master's degree at Harvard Kennedy School. Funded by HKS, Germany's ERP assets, the Haniel Foundation and others; launched in 1983. Applicants apply to Studienstiftung and Harvard Kennedy School simultaneously.
application_process: Download application form (German) from the McCloy programme page
Submit completed PDF application by email by November 1
Apply simultaneously and independently to Harvard Kennedy School
Shortlisted applicants invited to a selection seminar
Contact: mccloy@studienstiftung.de

scholarships.name: Studienstiftung Leo Baeck Fellowship
scholarships.provider: Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes / Leo Baeck Institute London / Simon Dubnow Institute
scholarships.program_type: International fellowship for German-Jewish history and culture doctoral research
application_period: Applications typically open in November – close February 1
important_dates: Shortlisted candidates invited to video interviews: April/May
Up to 10 fellows selected per year

raw_items: Open to doctoral candidates of any nationality at any university worldwide
Must be enrolled in a formal doctoral programme at an accredited university
Excellent university degree(s)
Last degree not before February 2022 (for 2026 cycle)
Research project must focus on history and culture of German-speaking Jewry (any period, region, field)
Fellows remain at their home institution during the fellowship
Cannot combine with scholarships from third parties

benefits: Additional living allowance for those doing doctorate outside home country
Tuition fee subsidy up to €10,000/year for non-home-country doctorates
Access to two joint workshops per year with international peers
Network access: Studienstiftung, Leo Baeck Institute London, Simon Dubnow Institute Leipzig
scholarships.target_group: Doctoral researchers of any nationality at any university worldwide whose dissertation focuses on German-Jewish history and culture - covering history, literature, philosophy, cultural studies from any period or region.
scholarships.description: The Leo Baeck Fellowship funds up to 10 international doctoral researchers annually for one year, supporting research into German-Jewish history and culture. Unique in being open to scholars at any university worldwide (not only German institutions). Run jointly by the Studienstiftung, Leo Baeck Institute London, and Leibniz-Institute Simon Dubnow Leipzig.
application_process: Submit a single PDF via email to leobaeck@studienstiftung.de
Required documents: application form, cover letter (1 page), CV, degree certificates, research proposal (max 5 pages), research schedule, 2 letters of recommendation
Deadline: February 1
Shortlisted candidates invited to two video interviews (April/May)
Contact: Dr Peter Antes - leobaeck@studienstiftung.de

scholarships.name: Holland Scholarship (NL Scholarship)
scholarships.provider: Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science / Dutch Universities
scholarships.program_type: Government-backed entry scholarship for non-EEA students
scholarships.deadline: Varies by university - typically January to April (for September intake). Applications open November 1.
important_dates: Deadlines vary per participating university - check individual university pages
One-time payment in first year only
NOT all Dutch universities participate - check the official participating list at studyinholland.nl/scholarships/holland-scholarship

raw_items: Nationality outside the European Economic Area (EEA) - Indonesian students are eligible
Applying for a bachelor's or master's at a PARTICIPATING Dutch university (not all universities participate - check the list)
Not previously studied in the Netherlands for a degree programme
Meet the individual university's additional requirements (GPA, language, etc.)

Participating universities include: TU Delft, University of Groningen, Leiden University, Utrecht University, University of Amsterdam (UvA), Erasmus University Rotterdam, Maastricht University, Radboud University, University of Twente, Wageningen University, and others - check the full list at studyinholland.nl
Each participating university sets its own secondary criteria and may offer a limited number of scholarships

benefits: €5,000 one-time payment in the first year of study
scholarships.target_group: Non-EEA international students applying for the first time to a bachelor's or master's programme at a participating Dutch research university or university of applied sciences.
scholarships.description: The Holland Scholarship is a €5,000 one-time award in the first year, jointly funded by the Dutch government and participating universities. Important: NOT all Dutch universities participate - you must first verify that your target university is on the official participating list at studyinholland.nl. Each participating university has its own application deadline (typically Jan–Apr) and may add its own eligibility conditions.
application_process: Step 1: Go to studyinholland.nl/scholarships/holland-scholarship and check the list of currently participating universities
Step 2: Apply for degree admission at a participating Dutch university
Step 3: Once you have an application or offer, apply for the Holland Scholarship through that university's own scholarship portal (not through Nuffic directly)
Step 4: Submit before the university's specific Holland Scholarship deadline (typically January–April, varies per university)
Applications open November 1 each year - deadlines vary per institution
Contact your target university's International Student Services or Scholarship Office to confirm participation and deadline for your cycle

scholarships.name: Orange Knowledge Programme (OKP)
scholarships.provider: Nuffic / Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs
scholarships.program_type: Government development scholarship for working professionals from developing countries
fields: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights
All fields aligned with Dutch development priorities
scholarships.deadline: Varies by course and institution - typically October to February for following year intake
application_period: Check Nuffic OKP portal for current cycle per institution
important_dates: Indonesia is an OKP eligible country
Applications open approximately October each year
NOT all Dutch institutions participate - only those listed on the Nuffic OKP portal
Check eligible institutions and courses at: https://www.nuffic.nl/en/subjects/orange-knowledge-programme

raw_items: Citizen AND current resident of an OKP-eligible country (Indonesia is eligible) - you cannot apply if you already live/work abroad
Currently employed as a working professional - NOT intended for recent graduates or students
Must be nominated or sponsored by your employer or a relevant organization - individual self-nominations are generally not accepted
Your employer must agree to grant leave of absence and a return guarantee after the scholarship
The chosen course/programme must be on the approved OKP list at a participating Dutch institution (not all Dutch universities are OKP partners)
English language proficiency: IELTS 6.0+ or equivalent (exact requirements vary per institution and programme)
Must commit to returning to your home country and employer after completing the programme
Priority given to professionals working in areas aligned with Dutch development priorities (water, food security, health, governance)

benefits: Monthly living allowance (amount varies by institution and programme)
Visa and Dutch residence permit costs
scholarships.target_group: Employed professionals from OKP-eligible developing countries (including Indonesia) who are nominated by their employer for a master's degree or short course at a participating Dutch institution in a development-relevant field.
scholarships.description: The Orange Knowledge Programme (OKP) is a fully funded Dutch government scholarship exclusively for employed professionals from developing countries (including Indonesia). You must be nominated by your employer and currently working - it is not open to students or recent graduates. Only specific courses at specific Dutch institutions are eligible; check the Nuffic OKP portal for the current approved list.
application_process: Step 1: Check the Nuffic OKP portal (nuffic.nl) to confirm Indonesia is eligible for the current cycle and find the list of approved courses and institutions
Step 2: Identify a specific approved course/programme at a participating Dutch institution
Step 3: Secure formal nomination and employer support (leave of absence + return guarantee)
Step 4: Apply through the OKP application portal on the Nuffic website - NOT directly through the Dutch institution
Step 5: Submit employer nomination letter, transcripts, CV, motivation letter, English language certificate
Contact Nuffic Indonesia office or check: nuffic.nl/en/subjects/orange-knowledge-programme

scholarships.name: Orange Tulip Scholarship (OTS)
scholarships.provider: Nuffic / Dutch Government / Participating Dutch Universities
scholarships.program_type: Country-specific scholarship for students from eligible countries including Indonesia
scholarships.deadline: Varies by university - typically January to April
application_period: Check individual Dutch university OTS pages for current cycle
important_dates: Indonesia is an OTS eligible country
Benefits vary per university: partial fee waiver to full scholarship - check each university's OTS page
Apply through individual Dutch universities, NOT centrally through Nuffic

Dutch universities offering OTS for Indonesia (recent years): TU Delft, University of Groningen, Leiden University, VU Amsterdam, Wageningen University, Rotterdam School of Management (Erasmus), HAN University, Saxion, The Hague University - list changes annually

raw_items: Indonesian citizen - currently residing in Indonesia (not already living abroad)
Applying for a bachelor's or master's at a PARTICIPATING Dutch university (check: nuffic.nl/en/scholarships/orange-tulip-scholarship)
Does not hold Dutch nationality or permanent Dutch residence permit
Meets the chosen university's academic admission requirements (GPA, language certificate)
Strong academic record - each university sets its own minimum threshold
Note: benefit amounts and eligibility criteria differ per university - e.g., TU Delft OTS may cover partial tuition only, while other universities may offer different packages
Typically cannot be combined with Holland Scholarship at the same university

benefits: Varies per university: partial tuition fee waiver, full tuition waiver, or tuition + living allowance contribution
Example: TU Delft OTS - partial tuition discount for Indonesian students
Example: VU Amsterdam OTS - fee waiver + monthly stipend contribution
Check each participating university's OTS page for exact current benefit amount
scholarships.target_group: Indonesian students (and other OTS-eligible nationalities) applying for bachelor's or master's programmes at participating Dutch universities, who want a partial or full tuition reduction.
scholarships.description: The Orange Tulip Scholarship is a country-specific scholarship initiative between the Dutch government and Dutch universities, available to students from eligible countries including Indonesia. Benefits and amounts vary significantly per university - from a partial fee discount to a full scholarship. You must apply through your target university directly, not through Nuffic. Always check the current participating university list for Indonesia at nuffic.nl.
application_process: Step 1: Go to nuffic.nl/en/scholarships/orange-tulip-scholarship and select Indonesia to see which Dutch universities are currently offering OTS for Indonesian students
Step 2: Choose a participating university and check their specific OTS page for eligibility, benefit amount, and application deadline
Step 3: Apply for degree admission at the chosen Dutch university first
Step 4: Submit the OTS application through the university's own scholarship portal (not through Nuffic directly)
Deadlines are set by each university individually - typically January to April for September intake
Contact the international admissions office of your target university for the current OTS application window

scholarships.name: Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarship - TU Delft
scholarships.provider: Justus & Louise van Effen Foundation / TU Delft
scholarships.program_type: Full excellence scholarship for international MSc students at TU Delft
fields: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science
important_dates: For MSc programmes starting the following September
Award value: €30,000 per year (covers tuition + living)
Highly competitive - typically ~20–30 awards per year across all TU Delft MSc programmes

raw_items: International student (non-Dutch) - EEA students may also apply but non-EEA students are strongly prioritised
Applying for any MSc programme at TU Delft
Exceptional academic track record - typically top of undergraduate class (cum laude or equivalent)
Must meet and fulfil all TU Delft MSc admission requirements independently
Note: you apply for admission AND the scholarship in parallel - do NOT wait for admission offer before applying for the scholarship
Application submitted via TU Delft's online application system (same portal as admission)
A separate scholarship motivation is required within the same application

benefits: €30,000 per year (covers tuition fee + living expenses)
Full scholarship for entire MSc duration (typically 2 years = €60,000 total)
scholarships.target_group: Outstanding international MSc applicants at TU Delft with exceptional academic achievement across engineering, technology, design, and applied sciences.
scholarships.description: The Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarship provides €30,000/year for the full 2-year MSc programme at TU Delft - one of the most generous university scholarships in the Netherlands. Application is made through the TU Delft online portal simultaneously with your MSc admission application. Deadline is December 1 annually. Highly competitive; typically top-of-class performance required.
application_process: Step 1: Go to tudelft.nl and start your MSc admission application via the TU Delft application portal
Step 2: Within the same application portal, indicate you want to apply for the van Effen Excellence Scholarship and complete the scholarship motivation section
Step 3: Submit the complete application (admission + scholarship) before December 1 at 23:59 CET
Step 4: If shortlisted, you may be invited for an online interview
Admission decisions and scholarship results are communicated separately
Official scholarship page: tudelft.nl/en/education/programmes/scholarships

scholarships.name: University of Groningen Excellence Scholarship
scholarships.program_type: Full merit scholarship for outstanding non-EEA international students
fields: All disciplines - one-year English-taught MSc programmes at RUG
scholarships.deadline: December 1 (for February intake) / February 1 (for September intake)
application_period: Check RUG scholarship page for programme-specific deadlines
important_dates: For September intake: apply by approximately February 1
For February intake: apply by approximately December 1
Award value: full tuition waiver + €11,000/year living allowance
Only available for one-year MSc programmes - not for two-year programmes
Not all RUG programmes offer this scholarship - check the RUG scholarship eligibility list

raw_items: Non-EEA nationality (EEA students are not eligible)
Applying for a one-year English-taught Master's programme at University of Groningen - NOT for two-year programmes
Outstanding academic record - typically top 10% of undergraduate cohort (GPA equivalent ~3.8/4.0 or 8.0+/10)
Must meet RUG's admission requirements for the specific programme
No previous RUG degree (cannot be a current or former RUG student)
Check which specific programmes are eligible: rug.nl/education/scholarships/university-of-groningen-scholarship

benefits: Total value approximately €22,000–€23,000 for a one-year programme
scholarships.target_group: Outstanding non-EEA international students in the top 10% of their undergraduate class applying for one-year English-taught Master's programmes at the University of Groningen.
scholarships.description: The University of Groningen Excellence Scholarship covers full tuition plus €11,000/year living allowance for outstanding non-EEA students. Important: only available for one-year programmes and not all RUG MSc programmes participate. Check the eligible programme list at rug.nl before applying.
application_process: Step 1: Verify your chosen RUG MSc programme is on the scholarship-eligible list at rug.nl/education/scholarships
Step 2: Apply for MSc admission via the RUG application portal (Studielink for EEA, direct portal for non-EEA)
Step 3: In your application, you will be automatically assessed for the scholarship based on your academic record - or submit a separate scholarship form if required by your programme
Step 4: Provide academic transcripts, CV, and motivation letter as part of the scholarship assessment
For September intake: apply before approximately February 1
For February intake: apply before approximately December 1
Contact: scholarships@rug.nl

scholarships.name: Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (AMS) - University of Amsterdam
scholarships.program_type: Top merit scholarship for outstanding non-EEA Master's applicants
fields: All disciplines - one-year English-taught Master's at UvA
scholarships.deadline: Varies by programme - typically January 15 (early) or February 1 (regular). Check UvA scholarship finder.
application_period: Approximately November – February for September intake
important_dates: Deadlines are programme-specific - check UvA scholarship finder at uva.nl
Only for one-year Master's programmes - not for two-year programmes
Note: Not all UvA MSc programmes offer AMS - check the eligible programme list
Very competitive - typically around 25 awards per year across all eligible UvA programmes

raw_items: Non-EEA nationality (EEA students are not eligible)
Applying for a one-year English-taught Master's programme at UvA - check programme eligibility at uva.nl/ams
Outstanding academic record - typically top 10% of undergraduate class (GPA equivalent ~3.8/4.0 or 8.0+/10)
Strong motivation and clear future potential
Must apply for UvA admission AND scholarship in the same application cycle - submit before the programme-specific scholarship deadline
Note: some UvA programmes use a separate AMS application form after admission; check your specific programme

benefits: Full tuition fee (varies by programme, typically €2,000–€18,000)
scholarships.target_group: Exceptional non-EEA international applicants in the top 10% of their class seeking a one-year Master's degree at the University of Amsterdam.
scholarships.description: The Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (AMS) is UvA's flagship scholarship for outstanding non-EEA Master's students, providing full tuition plus €25,000/year living allowance. Only available for one-year programmes and not all UvA MSc programmes are eligible. Around 25 awards per year across all eligible programmes - very competitive. Check uva.nl/ams for the current eligible programme list.
application_process: Step 1: Check which UvA Master's programmes offer AMS at uva.nl/en/education/master-s/scholarships-and-loans/amsterdam-merit-scholarship
Step 2: Apply for UvA Master's admission via the UvA application portal
Step 3: In the application portal, there will be a scholarship section - complete the AMS application (motivation letter and academic record) before the programme's scholarship deadline
Step 4: Submit before the programme-specific scholarship deadline (varies - typically January 15 or February 1)
Shortlisted candidates may be invited for an online interview
Contact: scholarships@uva.nl

scholarships.name: Leiden University Excellence Scholarship (LExS)
scholarships.program_type: Merit scholarship for outstanding non-EEA Master's students
fields: All disciplines - English-taught Master's at Leiden University
scholarships.deadline: Varies by programme - typically February 1 (for September intake). Check Leiden scholarship page.
application_period: Approximately November – February for September intake
important_dates: Must receive a conditional or unconditional admission OFFER before applying for LExS - unlike TU Delft, you cannot apply simultaneously
Three scholarship tiers - tier assigned based on academic excellence assessment
Does not include living allowance - tuition fee contribution only
Not all Leiden MSc programmes are eligible - check the programme-specific scholarship page

raw_items: Non-EEA nationality (EEA students are not eligible)
Must already hold a conditional or unconditional admission offer from Leiden University for an eligible Master's programme
Top 10% of current/most recent study programme (equivalent to ~8.0+/10 or 3.8/4.0 GPA)
Excellent academic record in all prior degrees
Check which Leiden programmes offer LExS at universiteitleiden.nl/en/education/scholarships

benefits: Tier 3: Full tuition fee minus the EEA/statutory rate
Important: tuition contribution ONLY - no living allowance included
amounts: €10,000 / €15,000 / full tuition minus EEA rate - tier depends on assessment
scholarships.target_group: Non-EEA international students in the top 10% of their class who have already received a Leiden University admission offer and are applying for an eligible English-taught Master's programme.
scholarships.description: The Leiden University Excellence Scholarship (LExS) offers tiered tuition fee contributions (€10k / €15k / full tuition minus EEA rate) - no living allowance. Key point: you must first receive an admission offer from Leiden before you can apply for LExS. Check which specific programmes participate, as not all Leiden Master's are eligible.
application_process: Step 1: Apply for Master's admission at Leiden University (apply early - November or December)
Step 2: Wait to receive a conditional or unconditional admission offer
Step 3: Once you have an admission offer, apply separately for LExS via the Leiden scholarship portal
Step 4: Submit transcripts showing top-10% ranking, a letter of recommendation, and a scholarship motivation statement
Step 5: Submit the LExS application before the programme's scholarship deadline (typically February 1)
Contact: international@leidenuniv.nl or check universiteitleiden.nl/en/education/scholarships

scholarships.name: Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship
scholarships.program_type: Full scholarship for outstanding non-EEA Master's students
fields: All disciplines - Master's programmes at Maastricht University
scholarships.deadline: February 1 (typical, for September intake) - confirm on UM scholarship portal
application_period: Check Maastricht University scholarship portal for current cycle
important_dates: Award covers full tuition + monthly living allowance for entire Master's duration
One of the only fully funded options for non-EEA students at UM

raw_items: Non-EEA nationality (EEA students are not eligible)
Applying for any Master's programme at Maastricht University - most programmes are eligible
Outstanding academic achievement: top 5% of undergraduate cohort (GPA equivalent ~3.9/4.0 or 9.0+/10)
